A hands-on, three-day **workshop** on **single-cell RNA-seq analysis** for biologists who already write a little R and have used the command line. Run as an in-person workshop at the University of Oregon — no tests, no homework, no grades, just three days of working through the modern scRNA-seq pipeline on your own laptop with the instructors next to you. An **optional Day 0** runs the day before for participants who want a refresher on R, the Unix command line, or Git before the workshop proper begins.

## What you'll do

Over three days you will work end-to-end through a standard scRNA-seq analysis:

- Load a 10x Cell Ranger output into Seurat and inspect it
- Run quality control (`nCount`, `nFeature`, `percent.mt`, doublets, ambient RNA)
- Normalize, find highly-variable genes, scale, run PCA, build a neighbor graph, cluster, and embed with UMAP
- Find cluster markers and assign cell-type labels by hand
- Integrate multiple samples with Harmony / Seurat anchors and diagnose over-correction
- Run condition-level pseudobulk differential expression with DESeq2
- Run functional enrichment (GO, GSEA, Reactome) with `clusterProfiler`
- Run differential abundance testing with `miloR`
- Use reference-based annotation with `SingleR` and Azimuth

The full Day-by-day plan is on the **[Schedule](Schedule.qmd)** page.

The workshop runs on the laptop-friendly `ifnb` dataset (\~14k cells, no 10x click-through). We use the **same `ifnb` dataset on both your laptop and on the Talapas HPC**, so you can complete the full pipeline without wrangling raw data or a separate dataset. For the workshop we **do not start the Talapas track from raw FASTQs**; instead, the Talapas materials show how to run the same `ifnb` analysis on UO's cluster — logging in, loading software modules, and **writing and submitting SLURM batch scripts**. The raw-FASTQ → Cell Ranger steps remain in the materials for self-paced exploration after the workshop. Bonus self-paced materials — scATAC-seq, WGCNA, spatial transcriptomics, and FAIR data sharing — are linked from the Schedule and ship alongside the workshop materials for you to explore on your own time.

## Who this workshop is for

You will get the most out of this workshop if you:

- Are a graduate student, postdoc, or researcher starting (or planning) a project that involves scRNA-seq
- Can write basic R — read a CSV, use the tidyverse pipe `|>`, write a function, install a CRAN package
- Have used a Unix command line at least a few times — `cd`, `ls`, `grep`, `wget`
- Have a laptop with at least 16 GB RAM and \~10 GB free disk

If you have **no R experience** or your **command-line skills are rusty**, plan to attend the optional **Day 0**, and skim:

- [Appendix A — R Programming Fundamentals](Resources_Folder/Appendix_A_R_Programming.html)
- [Appendix B — Unix & the Command Line](Resources_Folder/Appendix_B_Unix_Command_Line.html)
- [Appendix C — Single-Cell Biology Refresher](Resources_Folder/Appendix_C_SC_Biology_Refresher.html) — if molecular biology is rusty

## What you should do before Day 1

Run the **[Software Setup](Software_Setup.qmd)** workflow on the laptop you intend to bring. It installs R, RStudio, every package the workshop uses, and the small workshop dataset. Plan **30–60 minutes** the day before — not the morning of.

If something errors during setup, the [FAQ](FAQ.qmd) documents the issues that come up most often. If you cannot resolve the install yourself, the optional Day 0 session is the right place to bring it.

## A resource you keep — learning beyond the workshop

This site is built to outlast the three days in the room. Everything here stays online and free after the workshop ends, so you can use it as a **reference and a practice space** as you begin applying scRNA-seq to your own data:

- **Re-run every tutorial at your own pace.** The hands-on tutorials (01–08) and their long-form [chapters](Readings.qmd) stay available — come back to any step when you hit it in a real analysis.
- **Go further with the bonus tracks.** scATAC-seq, WGCNA, spatial transcriptomics, trajectory inference & cell–cell communication, and FAIR data sharing are self-paced modules you can work through whenever you're ready.
- **Scale up on Talapas.** The Talapas materials show how to move the same analysis onto UO's HPC on your own time.
- **Look things up.** The [Glossary](Resources_Folder/Glossary.html), prerequisite [appendices](Readings.qmd), [Additional Resources](Additional_Resources.qmd), and [FAQ](FAQ.qmd) are meant to be returned to long after the workshop is over.

Bookmark the site and treat it as a living reference — we expect you'll get as much out of it in the months *after* the workshop as during it.
